name: upgrade_pydantic_anystr_strip_whitespace_to_str_strip_whitespace
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: anystr_strip_whitespace=True to 2.x ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True) - the v1 key is silently ignored under pydantic 2.x, so string fields keep untrimmed surrounding whitespace; incomplete-fix broken switches to the ConfigDict container but keeps the stale v1 key name, so nothing actually changes
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Contact in contact.py uses the pydantic 1.x `class Config: anystr_strip_whitespace = True` pattern so every string field has its surrounding whitespace stripped automatically. Under the installed pydantic 2.x, this key is silently ignored (unrecognized), so name and city now keep their leading/trailing whitespace untouched. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: `model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` as a class attribute. Both name and city must have surrounding whitespace stripped after the fix.

test_setup_files.test_contact.py:
from contact import Contact

c = Contact(name="  Ada  ", city=" London ")
assert c.name == "Ada", f"name not stripped: {c.name!r}"
assert c.city == "London", f"city not stripped: {c.city!r}"

print("PASS")

reference_solution.contact.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Contact(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)

    name: str
    city: str

files.contact.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Contact(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(anystr_strip_whitespace=True)

    name: str
    city: str
